evals.name: feature-flag-talk
evals.prompt: I'm giving a 10-minute internal talk to our backend team next Thursday about how we roll out feature flags — we've had a couple incidents recently where someone flipped a flag globally and took prod down, so this is really about the process side, not the tooling. Probably like 8-12 slides? I want it to feel practical, engineers hate fluff, maybe a little irreverent if it works. I'll present on my laptop so nothing fancy is needed.
evals.expected_output: A slide deck (single HTML file) with 8-12 slides on feature-flag rollout process, plus numbered image-generation prompts.

assertions.text: Outputs include a single valid HTML file with DOCTYPE, <html>, <body>, and at least one <section class="slide"> element
HTML contains 8-12 slide sections
A separate artifact contains numbered image-generation prompts (at least 3), each several sentences of descriptive prose
HTML image references use relative paths like images/image_1.png
HTML includes viewport-fit CSS: scroll-snap-type on html, 100vh/100dvh on slides
HTML includes JS that binds keyboard events for navigation
The chosen font is NOT Inter
Deck focuses on the process/human side of rollouts (incidents, review, gradual rollout, kill switches) not generic 'why feature flags are good' content
Tone reads as practical and direct; no corporate marketing-speak

evals.name: hedge-pitch
evals.prompt: hey so im trying to pitch a side project to some angel investors, its a chrome extension called Hedge that scans your emails before you send and flags passive voice and hedging words like 'just' and 'i think' — basically helps people sound more direct. need a deck i can walk through on a zoom call, probably 8 slides, tone should be confident but not overclaimed because these are engineer-background VCs and theyll see through bullshit. happy to generate whatever images you ask for
evals.expected_output: An 8-slide investor pitch deck for a Chrome extension called Hedge, plus numbered image prompts.

assertions.text: Outputs include a single valid HTML file with DOCTYPE and slide sections
HTML contains 7-9 slide sections
A separate artifact contains numbered image-generation prompts (at least 3)
HTML image references use relative paths
HTML includes viewport-fit CSS
HTML has keyboard nav JS
The chosen font is NOT Inter
Deck covers problem, product, demo/mock, and an ask/CTA. Product name Hedge appears on title slide.
Tone is confident but grounded; no hockey-stick TAM claims without basis

evals.name: typography-critique
evals.prompt: Can you help me put together a design critique deck for our quarterly design review. Topic is typography choices in product UIs, specifically why everyone defaulting to Inter is actually a problem. Audience is 20 designers at my company, they're opinionated and know the fundamentals so don't dumb it down. I want it to feel opinionated and specific — I'm taking a position, not surveying the field. Maybe 12-15 slides. Visuals matter a lot here obviously since it's about type.
evals.expected_output: A 12-15 slide opinionated deck arguing against defaulting to Inter, plus image prompts relevant to typography.

assertions.text: Outputs include a single valid HTML file with DOCTYPE and slide sections
HTML contains 11-16 slide sections
A separate artifact contains numbered typography-specific image prompts
HTML image references use relative paths
HTML includes viewport-fit CSS
HTML has keyboard nav JS
The deck's chosen font is NOT Inter — using Inter in a deck arguing against Inter is a fatal self-own
Deck actively argues against Inter defaulting (thesis argument), not a neutral survey
Copy assumes design fluency; uses type terminology (x-height, counters, contrast, optical sizing, etc.) without explaining basics
